chapters.title: An upload needs an allowance
chapters.lead:
<rr-mermaid class="rr-diagram-delta">flowchart TD
 A[Account] --> H[Handler, changed]:::changed
 H --> S[Store]
 click A "rr:code/internal/upload/account.go"
 click H "rr:sym/ServeHTTP"
 click S "rr:sym/Store"</rr-mermaid>

steps.text: The service stores authenticated uploads immediately. The handler is the centre of this diff: it will join account identity, the bucket and the HTTP response.
Authentication supplies an account and its plan. The new allowance belongs to that account, so its users share one bucket.
The bucket refills with elapsed time, up to the plan’s burst capacity. Take spends a token or returns the wait for the next one.
Free allows one upload per second with a burst of two; Pro allows five with a burst of ten. The renamed configuration also lists Team. The loader decodes these settings.

chapters.title: The handler joins the contract
chapters.lead:
<rr-mermaid>flowchart TD
 P[Plan lookup] --> T[Take]
 T --> H[Handler]
 click P "rr:code/config/limits.json"
 click T "rr:sym/Take"
 click H "rr:sym/ServeHTTP"</rr-mermaid>

steps.text: The handler asks Take before storing a body. A rejected request receives 429 and a Retry-After value rounded up to whole seconds.
The client retries a 429 with the same payload. The handler supplies Retry-After, but the loop never waits; together these paths decide whether a rejected upload can recover.
High: Team uploads bypass the limit.
